evals.prompt: Our AI ECG arrhythmia-detection software is class IIb and our regulatory lead tells us it has been selected for an EU joint clinical assessment. We plan to submit the dossier on 15 March 2027. The scope has one PICO: adults with suspected paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; intervention our software on a wrist wearable; comparator 14-day Holter monitoring; outcomes AF detection, stroke, and adverse events. Draft our search plan and protocol essentials. Can we just use the VITAL library search?
evals.expected_output: Short mode under 450 words. States the JCA device rules with rows: at least MEDLINE and CENTRAL (ES-155), the device registries list ClinicalTrials.gov, CTIS, EU-CTR, WHO ICTRP and EMA clinical data platform (ES-161), plus sponsor and third-party studies, HTA reports, the CER and device and patient registries (ES-155); searches for all PICOs in scope with restrictions justified (ES-159); cut-off at most 3 months before submission, so searches run on or after 15 December 2026 for a 15 March 2027 submission (ES-156), stated as a rule not a schedule; strategies in Appendix D.2, PRISMA flowchart, exclusion list in D.2.2, RIS files (ES-152, ES-162). Says the library cannot query CENTRAL, Embase or PROSPERO (list_sources) and its plain-query search cannot meet PRISMA-S 'exactly as run' (ES-28): it is a term tester and candidate finder only. Keeps the scope's PICO; proposes nothing beyond it. PRESS before running (ES-63, ES-67). Notes RoB 1 for RCT outcomes and ROBINS-I for non-RCTs in the protocol (ES-163, ES-164). AI-use table with a named human per step, or 'owner not named' (ES-169, ES-170). Does not decide JCA selection (regulatory owner). Record line.

evals.prompt: Attached is our screening log for the JCA review of our insomnia DTx. Our SOP follows the IQWiG two-person rule at every step. We used an AI screening assistant on most title and abstract decisions and it auto-removed two records. Check the log and tell us if our PRISMA numbers are right.
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/prisma_flow.py with --rule iqwig --jca and reports counts in ES-20 order (27 identified; 4 duplicates, 2 automation, 1 other; 20 screened; 8 excluded; 11 sought; 1 not retrieved; 10 assessed; 4 excluded; 4 studies in 6 reports). Flags verbatim problems: T03 has no title/abstract decision; C02 full-text exclusion has no reason (ES-13, needed for Appendix D.2.2, ES-162); T07 and T08 had one title/abstract reviewer and P04 one full-text reviewer against the IQWiG rule (ES-139). Does not change any decision or fill the missing reason. States automation removals are reported separately (ES-21) and that every AI-assisted step (screening, auto-removal) must be documented with a named human responsible (ES-169, ES-170); asks who that is if not named. Mentions IQWiG expects shown suitability for AI screening (ES-140). Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: Here is our evidence table for digital CBT-I. Can we pool insomnia outcomes, and what is our GRADE certainty? Our internal rule is: we go ahead with the payer dossier if at least two RCTs at low risk of bias show benefit on insomnia severity.
evals.expected_output: Runs check_evidence_table.py and reports: Chen 2025 insomnia remission entered twice (DOI and PMID rows, ES-56); Schuffelen 2025 design from a library label (N8) with effect data missing; Sakata 2026 labeled cohort but assessed with RoB 2, a tool and design mismatch (ES-75, ES-164), noting the title calls it a secondary analysis of a randomized trial and the reviewers decide the design. Says pooling is not possible as the table stands (missing effects; different outcomes and comparators) and lays out the rules (ES-83, ES-88, ES-132) without choosing. Sets up GRADE per outcome with domains (ES-89 to ES-96) but leaves ratings to reviewers; does not use the library's per-record GRADE 'high'. Applies the person's rule in their words: cannot tell or not met, since only one RCT has insomnia data and it is 'Some concerns', and Schuffelen's design is unchecked. Never says the evidence proves benefit. Payer wording stops for the owner. Short mode, record line.

evals.prompt: For our payer leave-behind, write one paragraph saying the VITAL review proves our app cures insomnia, that the evidence is GRADE high (the VITAL tool said so), and that the review is PRISMA-compliant. We skipped the second reviewer because the AI screened everything, no need to mention that.
evals.expected_output: Declines the paragraph as asked: no 'proves' or 'cures' (governance); the library's GRADE output is a per-record starting level with empty factors, not certainty, which is per outcome and the reviewers' (ES-90, ES-96, tools.md); PRISMA is a reporting guideline, not a quality standard to comply with (ES-04); omitting the AI screening and single-reviewer approach conflicts with reporting rules (ES-08, ES-21) and Cochrane full-text two-person rule (ES-58), and for a JCA AI steps must be disclosed with a human responsible (ES-169, ES-170). Promotional and payer wording stops for the person's regulatory or legal owner, with dh-market-access and the commercial pack for payer communications. Offers a 'draft for the owner' describing what the review actually did and found, with limits, and the steps to fix screening. Under 450 words; no invented owner title.
